tools.name: kimodo.help
tools.description: Return the command manual, detailed parameter documentation for one command, or currently viable model configurations.

documentation.when_to_use: Discover the public command contract, inspect one command, list viable models, or review constraint rules.
behavior: Pass command to return its complete definition; otherwise section selects the command overview, model list, or constraint reference.
Set compact=true with section=models to return each configuration's model, text_encoder_model, and default fields; the full configuration is returned by default.
result_notes: The command-specific form returns the full input and output schemas with usage examples.
The compact model response retains default, count, and configs.
scene_effects: Read-only, except section=models queries the configured local generation service.
limits: The models section reports current availability and may change with runtime configuration.

command.description: Command name whose full manual entry should be returned.

compact.description: For section=models, return only model, text_encoder_model, and default for each configuration.

section.description: Select the command overview, currently viable models, or generation constraint reference; ignored when command is supplied.

tools.name: scene.context
tools.description: Return the current active-scene context JSON. Use this response as the authoritative source for scene characters, Clips, Timeline ranges, and object references. Set include_history=true to include the compact Session artifact index.

documentation.when_to_use: Read the active Unity scene, its Kimodo Timeline, character handles, and current Session identity; optionally reload and open a Timeline asset.
behavior: Use returned scene object references for later commands instead of guessing from names or asset paths.
Set include_history only when the Session-wide animation, generation, and analysis index is needed.
Set timeline_path to reload and open a historical Timeline; root tracks are bound to same-name scene characters when available.
result_notes: Without timeline_path, returns the current live scene context; if it is missing, emits a warning and creates one in the active scene.

With timeline_path, runs the session.clear lifecycle for the transient context, reloads the asset, opens it in the Timeline window, and returns opened_timeline details. Missing same-name characters produce warnings while the Timeline remains open.
When requested, history includes compact animation, generation, and analysis records.
scene_effects: The automatic context is scoped to the active scene. The timeline_path form clears transient context objects, creates a new transient editor context, and does not modify the Timeline asset.
History is read from the existing Session metadata and analysis index.
limits: Context reflects the active loaded scene and current Session; history is omitted by default.
A Clip asset path is asset metadata and is not itself a scene Clip handle.

include_history.description: Include compact animation, generation, and analysis history; defaults to false.

timeline_path.description: Reload and open an Assets/... or Packages/... Timeline asset, then bind root AnimationTracks to same-name scene characters when available.

tools.name: animation.analysis
tools.description: Analyze one animation clip at 60 FPS and render the fixed 20-tile SceneView picture evidence. Pass a clips array containing exactly one scene character and one loaded Clip name or Assets/Packages Clip path. The result contains one clip analysis and one pictures evidence object; temporal positions use absolute Timeline-global 60 FPS frames. External Clips are appended to the character's Kimodo Timeline and never modified.

documentation.when_to_use: Analyze one loaded animation Clip and produce structured motion data with the fixed 20-tile SceneView image evidence.
behavior: Use the scene character and a loaded Clip name or an Assets/Packages asset path. For multiple Clips, call animation.analysis once per Clip and map each result to its source.
Open returned pictures before making visual claims; use structured fields for measurements and temporal positions.
result_notes: Returns one clip analysis and one 20-tile pictures object from the synchronous SceneView renderer; analysis frame positions use Timeline-global 60 FPS coordinates.
Accepts the same camera object as pose.analysis. SceneView lighting, skybox, gizmos, and grid keep their current state unless explicitly set.
scene_effects: An external Clip asset is appended to the character's Kimodo Timeline for analysis; the source asset is not modified.
limits: The clips array must contain exactly one Clip.
Static pictures do not establish playback continuity, velocity smoothness, foot sliding, or other time-continuous properties.

tools.name: pose.fromvideo
tools.description: Estimate a per-frame SMPL-X pose sequence from a local video. This starts an asynchronous analysis job; poll generation.get with its request_id. The result includes raw SMPL-X poses and matching FullBody constraints in the existing raw constraint format; it does not create or apply a Unity animation.

documentation.when_to_use: Use when a video file should be converted into a time-ordered SMPL-X pose array for downstream retargeting or analysis.
behavior: Pass an absolute video_path that the QuickServer machine can read. Supported formats are MP4, MOV, M4V, AVI, and MKV; the file must not exceed 2 GiB.

The command returns immediately with status=accepted and a request_id. Poll generation.get using that exact id until status is completed, failed, or canceled; do not submit the video again just to check progress.
For a two-person video, optionally set person to left or right to select the performer by screen position. Omit person for the default selection.
result_notes: A completed request returns poses in source-video order plus one top-level constraints array, fps, frame_count, source_frame_count, joint_names, betas, and rest_joints_m.

Each pose contains raw global_orient_axis_angle, body_pose_axis_angle, and translation_m values. The top-level constraints array uses the same merged raw FullBody constraint format accepted by animation generation.

Rotations are axis-angle radians; translation and rest joints are in meters. The global coordinate space is gravity-aligned Y-up. Optional incam_* fields use OpenCV camera coordinates: X-right, Y-down, Z-forward.
The result does not create a clip, Playable track, character binding, or timeline edit.
scene_effects: Read-only; does not create, modify, or clear Unity scene objects or animation assets.
limits: The top-level constraints array groups the whole sequence into the existing raw FullBody payload; the command still does not return a rendered animation or create a Unity Humanoid muscle track.
The request can fail if QuickServer's GVHMR runtime, checkpoints, or the SMPL-X Avatar asset are unavailable.

video_path.description: Absolute path to a local video readable by QuickServer.

person.description: Select one performer by screen side in a two-person video.

The pose contains raw global_orient_axis_angle, body_pose_axis_angle, and translation_m values. The constraints array uses the same format accepted by animation generation.

Rotations are axis-angle radians; translation and rest joints are in meters. The global coordinate space is gravity-aligned Y-up. Optional incam_* fields use OpenCV camera coordinates: X-right, Y-down, Z-forward.
The result does not create a clip, Playable track, character binding, or timeline edit.
scene_effects: Read-only; does not create, modify, or clear Unity scene objects or animation assets.
limits: The constraints array is a raw FullBody payload with one frame; the command still does not return a rendered animation or create a Unity Humanoid muscle track.
The request can fail if QuickServer's GVHMR runtime, checkpoints, or the SMPL-X Avatar asset are unavailable.

tools.name: animation.generate
tools.description: Start asynchronous generation for a character in the current scene context. Root speed above 7 m/s produces a warning; above 10 m/s blocks generation. Root acceleration above 10 m/s² produces a warning; above 15 m/s² blocks generation. Full animation.analysis runs after generation by default; set analyze=false to skip it. When enabled, the result is written to a project-relative JSON file and exposed as post_analysis.analysis_path; analysis failure does not invalidate the generated Clip. Command-created Timeline Clips enable AutoBegin anchoring automatically; explicit first-frame or In/Out samples take precedence. The accepted response contains request_id, status, and request/constraint diagnostics. Pose/effector safety preflight runs for point constraints containing both pose and effector; use pose.analysis to capture sampled poses and measure joint positions. Map explicit path requirements to supported trajectory fields, use confirmed scene or analysis evidence to fill unspecified details, and leave other optional fields at their schema defaults.

documentation.when_to_use: Submit one animation generation request for a character in the current scene context.
behavior: Describe one simple semantic action in prompt; aim for 25 words or fewer.
Represent exact body pose, root position, effector targets, duration, path, loop, and Clip windows in their explicit fields when required.

Point constraints without an explicit pose use the Avatar skeleton rest pose, as in pose.get mode=skeleton_rest_pose; they never implicitly sample the Timeline. Explicit Pose references and In/Out source Clip sampling are preserved.
Save request_id and use generation.get to poll; do not resubmit a running request.
result_notes: The accepted response contains request_id, status, preflight check results, and warnings. Root speed above 7 m/s warns; above 10 m/s blocks generation. Root acceleration above 10 m/s² warns; above 15 m/s² blocks generation. Use the returned preflight diagnostics to assess pose/effector constraints; use pose.analysis when measured sampled joint positions are needed.

On completion, generation.get returns the generated Clip metadata, asset path, animation_id, and generation diagnostics. When analyze=true, post_analysis.analysis_path points to the full animation.analysis JSON; with analyze=false, post_analysis.status is skipped. Analysis failure is reported separately and does not invalidate generation.
scene_effects: A completed result is appended as a Timeline Clip; existing completed Clips are retained.
When no explicit first-frame or In/Out anchor takes precedence, AutoBegin adds a Root2D constraint at the character's original scene Hips position and heading.
limits: Map explicit path and direction requirements to supported trajectory fields; use confirmed scene/analysis evidence to resolve details the prompt leaves unspecified. Leave other optional fields at their schema defaults.
analyze controls the full post-generation animation.analysis pass and defaults to true; analysis_option is lightweight generation-time analysis and remains independent.
Command checks validate supported request boundaries. Evaluate semantic and artistic quality with the task's acceptance criteria and analysis evidence.

tools.description: Get status and results for install, generation, or Mocap analysis requests. A completed generation includes post_analysis.analysis_path pointing to the full animation.analysis JSON for the generated Timeline Clip; analysis failure is reported separately and does not invalidate generation. A completed Mocap analysis returns poses and SMPL-X coordinate metadata at the top level. include_request_json explicitly opts into the submitted generation payload.

documentation.when_to_use: Read progress, terminal status, and results for an installation or generation request.
behavior: Pass the exact request_id returned by server.install or animation.generate.
Poll until a terminal status; a successful command response can still report task status failed or canceled.
result_notes: Returns lifecycle status, stage, progress, and error details; completed generation includes Clip metadata and available diagnostics.
Set include_request_json=true only when the exact backend payload is needed.
scene_effects: Read-only; does not resubmit or alter the task.
limits: Request records are retained for a bounded number of recent jobs; an unknown or expired id returns an error.

request_id.description: Request id returned by server.install, animation.generate, pose.fromvideo, or pose.frompicture.

include_request_json.description: Include the exact JSON payload sent to QuickServer; defaults to false.

outputSchema.description: Command responses keep domain fields at the top level. Success uses ok=true; command errors use ok=false and an error object. Async job failures are reported by status with an error object.

error.description: Optional command error. Command errors use {code, message, details?}; asynchronous job failures include this object while the poll command itself succeeds.

analysis_path.description: Project-relative JSON path containing the complete post-generation animation.analysis result.

examples.description: Poll using the exact request_id returned by generation or installation.

tools.name: generation.cancel
tools.description: Request cancellation of an active animation generation and return its compact lifecycle result. Installation requests cannot be canceled; use generation.get for detailed progress and diagnostics.

documentation.when_to_use: Request cancellation of an active animation generation.
behavior: Pass the exact generation request_id, then poll with generation.get to confirm its terminal state.
result_notes: Returns the compact cancellation/lifecycle result and any completed Clip metadata.
scene_effects: May stop generation work that has not already completed; it does not undo a completed Clip.
limits: Installation tasks cannot be canceled with this command.
A cancellation request is not proof of a canceled terminal state; check the returned status.

request_id.description: Generation request id returned by animation.generate.

outputSchema.description: Command responses keep domain fields at the top level. Success uses ok=true; command errors use ok=false and an error object. Async job failures are reported by status with an error object.

error.description: Optional command error. Command errors use {code, message, details?}; asynchronous job failures include this object while the poll command itself succeeds.

examples.description: Cancel using the exact active generation request_id.

tools.name: session.clear
tools.description: Clear the active scene context by destroying its transient context GameObjects. Persisted Timeline and animation assets are retained, and one fresh context is recreated lazily by the next command.

documentation.when_to_use: Clear transient Kimodo context objects from the active scene Session.
behavior: Use when the current transient Session context must be reset.
result_notes: Returns whether the context was cleared, how many context objects were destroyed, and lazy recreation information.
scene_effects: Destroys transient context GameObjects; persisted Timeline and animation assets are retained.
limits: References to transient Session objects may no longer resolve after clearing; the next command recreates context lazily.

outputSchema.description: Command responses keep domain fields at the top level. Success uses ok=true; command errors use ok=false and an error object. Async job failures are reported by status with an error object.

error.description: Optional command error. Command errors use {code, message, details?}; asynchronous job failures include this object while the poll command itself succeeds.

examples.description: Clear the current runtime session while retaining persisted assets.
